states.unreviewed: No type-specific audit has been recorded for this profile, position and path.
states.inspected: Implementation was read; this is not an executed test.
states.passed: The named check passed for the recorded scope and artifact.
states.limited: The check covers only the explicitly recorded subset.
states.rejected: The path explicitly rejects this shape. Required delivery remains outstanding.

copied.ownership: Copied values have no retained Lean identity. Host-owned buffers may require a generated cleanup function.
copied.absence: No implicit null, omission or default conversion. Unit, Option, optional parameters and host null are separate cases.
copied.failure: Reject invalid host values before calling Lean. Preserve declared errors and unexpected-failure policy.

identity.ownership: Preserve nominal identity, runtime and generation. Generate borrow, lease, transfer and deterministic disposal from the declared lifetime.
identity.absence: A missing or disposed resource is not a null value. Optional identity values require an explicit Option mapping.
identity.failure: Reject stale, wrong-kind and wrong-runtime values. Cleanup must also run on callback re-entry and failure.

signature.ownership: Preserve every argument and result ownership transition, including cleanup after rejection or cancellation.
signature.absence: Keep parameter omission, declared defaults, Option.none and host null distinct.
signature.failure: Preserve declared errors, effect order and delivery protocol; reject unsupported signatures before producing a release.

erased.ownership: Proof-only values have no host allocation or handle.
erased.absence: Erasure is determined by elaborated Lean types, not by substituting null for an unknown type.
erased.failure: Keep runtime refinement checks and theorem provenance even when proof arguments are erased.

shapes.bounds: One inhabitant. A result with no host return value still requires an explicit argument and field mapping.
Exactly two Boolean values; do not coerce numbers or strings.
0..255; reject overflow before narrowing.
0..65535; reject overflow before narrowing.
0..4294967295, including on hosts with 32-bit signed integers.
0..18446744073709551615; no conversion through a floating-point host number.
-128..127; reject overflow before narrowing.
-32768..32767; reject overflow before narrowing.
-2147483648..2147483647; reject overflow before narrowing.
No fixed bit-width limit. Reject negative inputs and enforce documented allocation limits.
Preserve sign and magnitude without narrowing; enforce documented allocation limits.
Round to binary32. Specify NaN, infinities and signed zero; do not claim NaN payload preservation without a bit-level test.
Preserve binary64 values, NaN classification, infinities and signed zero.
Preserve Unicode scalar values and embedded NUL. Reject invalid encodings; declare byte and allocation limits.
Each byte is 0..255. Preserve zero bytes and owned result storage; declare copy limits.

shapes.meaning: An ordered, finite sequence of values.
shapes.bounds: Validate every element recursively, length and allocation limits. Array UInt32 alone does not cover Array α.
Keep none, some unit and nested options distinct; do not flatten them all to null.

shapes.meaning: A success value or a declared error value.
shapes.bounds: Preserve the success/error branch and both payload types. Lower Except ε α to IR result arguments [α, ε], in success/error order.

shapes.meaning: A fixed ordered product of values.
shapes.bounds: Preserve arity, nesting and per-position types; do not infer tuples from arbitrary arrays.

shapes.meaning: A named copied product with declared fields.
shapes.bounds: Preserve every field and mutability rule. A Payload example is not evidence for arbitrary records.

shapes.meaning: A named reference to another semantic type.
shapes.bounds: Resolve aliases without losing constraints, identity or ownership; reject alias cycles.

shapes.meaning: One named constructor with its typed fields.
shapes.bounds: Preserve constructor identity and payloads without exposing Lean constructor numbers.

shapes.meaning: A nominal value retained in the shared runtime.
shapes.bounds: Preserve cross-component identity and explicit disposal; reject stale or foreign resources.

shapes.meaning: A host callable with a declared signature and lifetime.
shapes.bounds: Preserve argument/result types, re-entry, invocation count, self-disposal and errors.
Preserve order, duplicates and nesting with a distinct list constructor. Validate all elements and copying limits; never expose Lean cons cells.
0..0x10FFFF excluding 0xD800..0xDFFF; not one UTF-16 code unit or an arbitrary string.
Bind width to the compiled Lean target, not the consumer process; reject out-of-range values.
Bind signed width to the compiled Lean target and record architecture explicitly.

shapes.meaning: A natural value strictly below a bound.
shapes.bounds: Keep the bound and validate it before erasing proof fields. Fin 0 has no constructible value.

shapes.meaning: A value satisfying a Lean predicate.
shapes.bounds: Generate a checked constructor when validation is executable; require explicit decisions for non-decidable predicates.

shapes.lean: Checked records and closed Nat indices
shapes.meaning: A structure with runtime payload fields and erased proofs, optionally specialized at closed Nat literal indices.
shapes.bounds: Construct inputs only through the selected safe Lean constructor over the exact payload fields. Preserve closed indices and per-site choices; project proof-backed results without fabricating proofs.

shapes.meaning: A runtime type or constraint depends on an earlier value.
shapes.bounds: Preserve the dependency through a checked lowering or a reviewed exclusion; never discard it as an implicit argument.
Bound nesting and allocation; reject host cycles unless the declared identity model supports them.

shapes.meaning: Exports parameterized by types or instances.
shapes.bounds: Deliver checked finite specializations; record open-generic gaps without using an untyped transport.
Separate erased type arguments from implicit runtime values; resolve them from elaborated information.
Specialize or supply the selected dictionary without changing runtime behavior.

shapes.meaning: Proof-only declarations and arguments are erased at runtime.
shapes.bounds: Record theorem identity and assumptions. Erasure does not remove the need to check a runtime refinement.

shapes.meaning: A callable permits an omitted argument.
shapes.bounds: Apply only the declared default; distinguish omitted input from a supplied Option.none.

shapes.meaning: Null from a declared host API.
shapes.bounds: Select an explicit host projection; null does not stand for every missing, erased or unsupported value.

shapes.meaning: A Lean action with IO effects and IO errors.
shapes.bounds: Executing IO is not automatically asynchronous. Preserve effect order and exceptions.

shapes.meaning: An effectful action with a declared error type.
shapes.bounds: Preserve typed failures separately from transport validation and unexpected traps.
Project every declared error and payload; preserve trap or poisoned-runtime handling separately.

shapes.meaning: A computation whose result arrives later.
shapes.bounds: Keep completion, rejection, cancellation and runtime lifetime distinct; do not block a browser event loop.

shapes.meaning: An identity-bearing object owned by the host.
shapes.bounds: Generate typed members and preserve receiver identity, dynamic-access policy and lifetime.

shapes.lean: Lean function returned to the host
shapes.meaning: A retained Lean closure callable through a generated host API.
shapes.bounds: Preserve captured state, call signature, errors and deterministic disposal.

shapes.meaning: A declared request to stop pending work.
shapes.bounds: Specify acknowledgement and late completion; release pending work exactly once.

shapes.meaning: A sequence delivered by explicit pulls.
shapes.bounds: Preserve values, end-of-sequence, failure, early return and cleanup.

shapes.meaning: A sequence whose individual pulls can complete later.
shapes.bounds: Preserve backpressure, pending-pull cancellation and terminal cleanup.

analysis.note: Prepared CPAN archives expose named constructor classes with keyword payloads. Both ordinary-source and independently reviewed builds install offline across all four pinned Perl ABIs, relocate and execute twice without compilers after author and handoff removal. Each execution passes 53,680 assertions over 4,226 calls with 116 rejected inputs and recovery. Isolated compiled XS probes exercise all eighteen constructors, recover from 494 conversion failures and 64 partial-input rejections, preserve four host exceptions, reject seven malformed tags before accessors and handle three reentrant field mutations. All twenty-four installed files retain their hashes through relocation and execution. Independent builds reproduce original archives and installed payloads; Perl installation metadata contains local paths and timestamps.

conversionNotes.variant: Construct values with Family::Case->new(field => value). Calls require exact generated classes and fields. Empty constructors and undef Unit payloads stay distinct. Compiler-owned helpers construct variants and read active payloads without exposing native constructor numbers or object layouts. Invalid tags reject before getters; scoped cleanup releases partial conversions on exceptions.

Local Linux x86-64, Wasmtime 42.0.1, wasm-tools 1.245.1, glibc floor 2.36; CI floor 2.38.

limitations: Linux x86-64 native Lean host and pinned Wasmtime 42.0.1; this is not a standalone WASI command. Lean words are 64-bit while canonical component memory uses wasm32 addresses.

Types are limited to 32 levels. Host conversions and native copying each have a 16 MiB accounting budget, and component scratch memory is capped at 64 MiB. These limits do not bound all Lean or Wasmtime working memory.

Callers supply valid C storage. Wasmtime allocation APIs do not offer recoverable out-of-memory errors. List callback payloads, resources inside copied values and recursive variants remain unsupported.

conversionNotes.list: Canonical WIT lists preserve empty sequences, order, duplicates and nesting; Lean List and Array retain distinct IR and native types. Public Wasmtime values borrow inputs and return independent owned copies, including nested branches, fields and bytes. Delete results with wasmtime_component_val_delete; they remain valid after closing the session. Preflight rejects wrong element types, missing buffers, excessive counts and invalid branches before Wasmtime copies input. Errors leave the output slot unchanged; trapped stores are replaced before reuse.

limitations: Pinned PHP-Wasm 0.1.0, PHP 8.4.1 NTS, Emscripten 3.1.68 and wasm32 in Node and Chromium. Synchronous primitive callables use the main execution context. The pinned host cannot start Fibers; its guard is tested separately in native PHP.
No compound callable, resource, async, copied-field or other-profile promotion. Host functions borrow one call; returned closures own a Zend resource with idempotent close and destructor fallback.

PHP, Zend and native copy budgets each limit conversions to 16 MiB. Brick Math text is limited to 16384 decimal digits. Reentry allows 64 invocations per adapter, with 4096 shared-runtime owned identities. These are not Lean/PHP heap limits.

conversionNotes.unit: Unit is null for arguments and results, including callbacks; a PHP void callback returns null.
conversionNotes.uint32: The 32-bit PHP host requires Brick\Math\BigInteger for the full 0..4294967295 range, even for small values; PHP ints, floats and numeric strings reject.
conversionNotes.int64: Exact Brick\Math\BigInteger preserves both signed 64-bit endpoints on the 32-bit host.
conversionNotes.nat: Exact Brick\Math\BigInteger; negative Nat inputs and callback results reject. No native integer narrowing.
conversionNotes.int: Exact signed Brick\Math\BigInteger including multi-thousand-bit captured values.
conversionNotes.char: One UTF-8 Unicode scalar, including NUL and supplementary values. Malformed text and multiple scalars reject.
conversionNotes.usize: Exact Brick\Math\BigInteger for the 32-bit compiled Lean target, checked in 0..4294967295.
conversionNotes.isize: PHP int for the 32-bit compiled Lean target, checked in -2147483648..2147483647.

limitations: Pinned PHP-Wasm 0.1.0, PHP 8.4.1 NTS, Emscripten 3.1.68 and wasm32 in Node and Chromium. Synchronous primitive callables use the main execution context. The pinned host cannot start Fibers; its guard is tested separately in native PHP.
No compound callable, resource, async, copied-field or other-profile promotion. Host functions borrow one call; returned closures own a Zend resource with idempotent close and destructor fallback.

PHP, Zend and native copy budgets each limit conversions to 16 MiB. Brick Math text is limited to 16384 decimal digits. Reentry allows 64 invocations per adapter, with 4096 shared-runtime owned identities. These are not Lean/PHP heap limits.

conversionNotes.closure: Invokable LeanClosure with exact positional arity, close and isClosed. Saved callable aliases share its lease. Cloning, serialization and direct construction reject.

conversionNotes.nat: Exact Brick\Math\BigInteger; negative Nat inputs and callback results reject. No native integer narrowing.
conversionNotes.int: Exact signed Brick\Math\BigInteger including multi-thousand-bit captured values.
conversionNotes.char: One UTF-8 Unicode scalar, including NUL and supplementary values. Malformed text and multiple scalars reject.
conversionNotes.usize: Exact Brick\Math\BigInteger for the 32-bit compiled Lean target, checked in 0..4294967295.
conversionNotes.isize: PHP int for the 32-bit compiled Lean target, checked in -2147483648..2147483647.

observations.scope: Prepared native Composer packages from ordinary source and independent reviewed IR preserve Option, Except and nested binary products, including nineteen primitives, arrays and copied record fields. Weak and strict callers each pass 46123 public assertions three times after offline installation and relocation, without producer sources, handoff archives or compilers. A separate in-memory probe injects 355 conversion failures per path, checks three real cleanup failures, seven malformed outputs and three inactive payloads. Installed files and mapped library hashes remain unchanged. PHP 8.2.33 NTS CLI, Linux x86-64; local glibc floor 2.36, CI 2.38. PHP-Wasm remains unpromoted.

limitations: Native PHP 8.2+ NTS CLI on Linux x86-64 only; PHP-Wasm, FPM and ZTS are not promoted.
Type nesting stops at 32. Validation, PHP conversion and shared native input/output copying each have a 16 MiB accounting limit, not a total-allocation bound.
Copied values cannot contain resources or callbacks. Compound callables, lists, tagged variants and recursive copied types remain separate work.

conversionNotes.option: None is null; new Some($value) retains presence. Some(null) preserves present Unit or an outer Some containing None, according to the declared payload type. Some(Some(null)) preserves two layers. Generated final readonly branch classes expose one value property. Concrete payloads are validated on every call, without weak-caller coercion.
conversionNotes.result: Lean Except E T becomes new Ok($value) or new Err($error), each exposing a readonly value property. Branch identity is preserved even for same-typed payloads. Domain errors return Err; bridge failures throw. PHP === compares object identity; PHP == property comparison is not generated Lean equality.
conversionNotes.tuple: Exactly two consecutive integer-key array elements preserve binary nesting and per-position validation. Nested arrays, records and branch payloads are copied independently. Validation, host conversion and native copying each have a 16 MiB accounting limit, not a bound on all PHP or Lean allocations. Payloads use the selected target's integer mappings.

conversionNotes.option: None is nil; Some.new(value) retains presence. Some.new(nil) represents an outer Some of an inner None; Some.new(UNIT) preserves present Unit. Some is a frozen Data class with equality and pattern matching. Concrete payload types are validated at the call; nil is valid only in Option positions.
conversionNotes.result: Lean `Except E T` becomes Ok.new(value) or Err.new(error), both exposing value. Exact branch classes preserve success/error identity, including same-typed payloads. Frozen Data wrappers support equality and patterns. Domain errors return Err; bridge failures raise.
conversionNotes.tuple: Exactly two Array elements, preserving binary nesting and per-position validation. Inputs are copied; returned arrays and strings own independent storage. Branch wrapper fields are frozen, but nested mutable payloads are not. Generated record classes compare fields by value within the same record class.

This observation covers copied acyclic values, nesting at most 32. Primitive callables, Char and platform words have separate installed evidence. Optional values, variants, resources and async remain outside this profile.

PHP and Zend conversions and native copying have separate 16 MiB accounting budgets. PHP lists count at least 32 bytes per element; Brick\Math\BigInteger canonical decimal text is limited to 16384 digits. These limits do not bound Lean working memory.

conversionNotes.unit: Unit is null in arguments, results and fields.
conversionNotes.bool: Exact bool in weak and strict callers; numbers and strings are not Boolean inputs.
conversionNotes.uint64: Brick\Math\BigInteger::of preserves the full unsigned range without conversion through PHP float.
conversionNotes.nat: Brick\Math\BigInteger accepts nonnegative integer values up to 16384 decimal digits.
conversionNotes.int: Brick\Math\BigInteger accepts signed integer values up to 16384 decimal digits.
conversionNotes.float32: PHP float input rounds to binary32 in scalar, array and record positions. NaN classification, infinities, subnormals and signed zero are checked.
conversionNotes.float64: Binary64 values, NaN classification, infinities, subnormals and signed zero are checked in scalar, array and record positions.
conversionNotes.string: Validated UTF-8 PHP strings preserve embedded NUL.
conversionNotes.bytes: Bytes::fromString and toString preserve arbitrary binary bytes.
conversionNotes.array: Consecutive-key PHP lists with recursive element validation; nested results own independent copies.
conversionNotes.record: Final readonly typed classes, including empty and scalar-represented records. Nested fields are checked and results own independent copies.
conversionNotes.uint32: The compiled copied API uses Brick\Math\BigInteger for the full 0..4294967295 range, even for values below PHP_INT_MAX. PHP ints, floats and numeric strings are rejected.
conversionNotes.int64: The compiled copied API uses Brick\Math\BigInteger for the full -9223372036854775808..9223372036854775807 range on the 32-bit host.

observations.scope: Prepared PHP-Wasm npm and Composer packages from ordinary source and independent reviewed IR preserve Option, Except and nested binary products, including all nineteen primitives, arrays and copied record fields. Each path runs twelve Node/Chromium, embedded/Composer/bundled, startup/lazy and weak/strict arrangements twice, with 46162 assertions per run. Offline installs use empty caches and repeat locked installs; producer, install workspace and archive handoff are removed before compiler-free execution. Installed file hashes remain unchanged and browser requests match deployment bytes. Separate synthetic Zend probes check 19 allocation failures, nine malformed outputs, three inactive payloads and two bailout recoveries in each caller mode. PHP-Wasm 0.1.0, PHP 8.4.1 and Emscripten 3.1.68, wasm32.

conversionNotes.option: None is null; new Some($value) retains presence. Some(null) preserves present Unit or an outer Some containing None, according to the declared payload type. Some(Some(null)) preserves two layers. Generated final readonly branch classes expose one value property. Concrete payloads are validated on every call, without weak-caller coercion.
conversionNotes.result: Lean Except E T becomes new Ok($value) or new Err($error), each exposing a readonly value property. Branch identity is preserved even for same-typed payloads. Domain errors return Err; bridge failures throw. PHP === compares object identity; PHP == property comparison is not generated Lean equality.
conversionNotes.tuple: Exactly two consecutive integer-key array elements preserve binary nesting and per-position validation. Nested arrays, records and branch payloads are copied independently. Validation, host conversion and native copying each have a 16 MiB accounting limit, not a bound on all PHP or Lean allocations. Payloads use the selected target's integer mappings.

An independent rebuild reproduces archives, loaded libraries and installed payloads; installation path metadata is excluded from the payload comparison.

An independent rebuild reproduces all original archives, installed files and public observations.

observations.scope: Original CPAN archives preserve eight acyclic copied shapes in callbacks and returned closures on ordinary-source and independently reviewed paths across all four pinned Perl ABIs. Each installation passes 64983 public assertions, 1686 calls and 325 rejected inputs. A separate XS probe verifies 22362 injected Perl exceptions, 160 scenarios and four deferred-close cases with no remaining registered owners. Exact consumer documentation and original installed APIs execute twice after relocation and producer-handoff removal. Fresh primitive, collection, compound, List and variant regressions pass on all four ABIs.

observations.scope: Original npm component and runtime archives preserve all nine copied shapes, including recursive values, in callbacks and returned closures on ordinary-source and reviewed-IR paths in Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit page/React/worker contexts. Each public consumer passes 133120 structured checks, 53 rejection cases and 8084 primitive checks. Archives are verified and relocated; producer sources and builds are deleted before offline, compiler-free installation. Exact consumer documentation executes twice per path. Separate compiled fault probes cover copied-output ownership and shared scalar/structured lifetime limits.

analysis.note: Native-backed WIT/WASI packages preserve all eight acyclic copied callback shapes on both source paths. Each installed consumer passes 470573 checks with 3911 calls, 3493 callbacks, 52 rejections and 401 finalizers, then repeats after the handoff is removed. Six loaded libraries and all installed files keep their verified identities. Separate mixed aliased/plain callbacks pass 56065 checks per path. Executable Lean/C documentation runs twice from each installed archive. ASan/UBSan and allocation-failure probes pass 70148 checks with zero tracked allocations left live and reject both ownership mutations. Fresh primitive regressions and complete predecessor code-generation comparisons preserve older APIs.

observations.scope: Prepared C/C++ packages preserve finite recursive copied callbacks and captured closures on ordinary-source and independently reviewed paths. Each C path passes 10207 public checks plus 217706 fault checks with 1974 native and 5328 GMP-facade allocation failures; each C++ path passes 14073 checks with 8992 injected host allocation failures. Sanitized runtime-only deployments remove all sources, headers and handoff archives. Mixed C/C++ consumers use both include orders and share one runtime with no leaked identities. Depth boundaries, malformed values, active disposal, expired creator threads, executable documentation and negative ownership mutations are checked.

Each installation passes 206 threaded or 204 unthreaded recursive checks, 64983 acyclic checks, 39045 injected failures, nine reply-owner checks and malformed-output retirement probes. Removing ownership or retirement protection produces the expected normal Perl exception before unsafe copying. Lifetime checks cover closure capacity, stale handles, deferred close, finalization and isolated fork-child cleanup. Exact publisher and consumer examples compile and run. All original installed files remain unchanged.

limitations: Perl 5.36.3 and 5.38.2, threaded and unthreaded, on little-endian Linux x86-64. Native reentry is bounded at 64 active calls; owned closures share 4096 identity slots.

conversionNotes.recursive: Recursive records, variants and aliases retain their public representations and independent copied storage. conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

observations.scope: Ordinary-source npm packages keep closed Fin bounds at top-level and structural-container parameters and results in browser pages, React effects and dedicated workers. generation.note: The generated JavaScript validates every constrained leaf before Wasm dispatch, and the compiled C adapter entry runs an exported Lean validator per refined parameter, including a top-level scalar Fin, before any dispatch; a direct runtime call with an out-of-bound value fails with the ABI's call status. compilation.note: The C adapter entry fails the call before the typed Lean wrapper or the source runs; the wrapper's own bound guard is not reached from any runtime entry. Generated Lean constructs Fin only inside the decidable check and projects results after the source call.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.checked-record: Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call.

Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

checked-record.parameter: Generated record dataclass with int and tuple payload fields; also carries the tested proof-free inherited Span, Ticket and Stamped record chain with nested parent subobjects preserved; also carries the tested proof-free recursive Packet and Envelope/Step graphs with nominal identities and active variants preserved

conversionNotes.checked-record: Pass the generated record's runtime payload fields, without proof values. The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested frozen Packet dataclass carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as exact Python int values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Python adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call.

conversionNotes.checked-record: Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. Generated frozen dataclasses carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C#, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: Unit, bool, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, sbyte, short, int, long, BigInteger for Nat and Int, float, double, string, byte[], Rune, ulong for USize and long for ISize. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.

conversionNotes.subtype: In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection.

conversionNotes.subtype: Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages.

conversionNotes.subtype: In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.

conversionNotes.subtype: In PHP-Wasm, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations on wasm32: null for Unit; bool; PHP int for UInt8, UInt16, Int8, Int16, Int32 and ISize; Brick\Math\BigInteger for UInt32, UInt64, Int64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float; string for String and Char; and generated Bytes for ByteArray. USize and ISize use 32-bit ranges. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, wrong host types, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, refused non-finite floats and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. Recursive Chain values use generated variant classes. PHP-Wasm traverses only the active case, checks each present Subtype with the constructor selected for that parameter, checks each Fin 3 digit, preserves shared caller graphs on rejection, and rejects cycles or values deeper than 128 copied levels. Results omit proof fields and input constructor choices.

Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call.
